messages:
jamie: heads-up — main CI red after i ran a lockfile regen for a deps cleanup. poetry pulled SQLAlchemy 2.2.0 and the integration tests for db fixtures are failing. job: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234

rian: which test(s) are failing? can you paste the stack / failing assertion?

jamie: paste of failing snippet:
```
ERROR: test_user_repo_create (tests.integration.test_user_repo::TestUserRepo)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/src/tests/integration/test_user_repo.py", line 42, in test_user_repo_create
    repo.create(user)
  File "/src/redwood/db/repo.py", line 78, in create
    res = self.session.execute(stmt)
  File "/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/result.py", line 122, in scalars
    raise TypeError('NoneType not iterable')
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable
```
Repro locally with `tox -e py39-integration` after `poetry lock && poetry install`. Downgrading to sqlalchemy==2.1.8 makes the tests pass locally.

dee: hm that smells like a SQLAlchemy API change (result handling) or a transitive helper that expects the old Result API. Did the lock regen also bump alembic / sqlalchemy-utils / databases?

jamie: short excerpt from poetry.lock: 
```
[[package]]
name = "sqlalchemy"
version = "2.2.0"
...
[[package]]
name = "alembic"
version = "1.11.0"
requires = ["sqlalchemy>=2.2"]
```
So alembic forced the newer SQLAlchemy in this env. I'm not sure which upstream prompted the bump.

rian: two options: quick rollback pin to 2.1.x in pyproject + regen lock, or fix tests/code to be compatible with 2.2 (likely change to using `scalars().first()` or adapting session.execute usage). Given this is a wide API change, i'd prefer rollback and then plan for compatibility work.

ops-bot: @jamie i scheduled a rerun of the failing job with fresh build (job 1234 -> 1237).

ci-bot: rerun finished: job 1237 still red, same stack. other suites are green.

dee: i can run a quick bisect: `git bisect` on lock regen doesn't help, but we have a lock-bisect script in infra/tools/bisect_lock.py that tries earlier lockfiles. i'll run against the main branch and see what pulled alembic to 1.11.0.

jamie: thanks. i'm going to open a tiny PR that pins sqlalchemy = "^2.1.0" in pyproject.toml and force `poetry lock` so CI doesn't pick 2.2 for now. will add a note in the PR to track follow-up to test against 2.2 (we should run the integration suite against both). pinging @rian for review.

rian: ack — if you add a short comment in the PR explaining this is temporary and link to this thread, i’ll approve quickly. also add a changelog entry in infra/lock-notes.md so we remember.

dee: update: bisect script says alembic 1.11 came in via `migrations-utils` bump in transitive deps; looks like `migrations-utils` just released 0.8.0 which tightened SQLAlchemy requirement. filing issue with them.

jamie: perfect. i'll open the rollback PR now. thanks all. :thumbsup:

rian: also let's add a CI job matrix item to run integration tests with SQLAlchemy 2.2 on a schedule (nightly) so we catch this earlier next time.

jamie: good idea — created follow-up ticket `ENGINFRA-412` and assigned to dee.

ops-bot: Created PR #2789 by jamie: "pin sqlalchemy to 2.1.x to avoid breakage from alembic/migrations-utils bump"

jamie: leaving this thread open until PR is merged and bisect follow-up done. thanks everyone!
